subsystems.name: Identifier layer
subsystems.role: assigns and resolves unique, cryptographically controlled identifiers to agents.

subsystems.name: Credential layer
subsystems.role: issues tamper-evident claims about an agent's provenance, capabilities, and permissions.

subsystems.name: Agent-side wallet
subsystems.role: holds the agent's private keys and presents credentials when challenged.

subsystems.name: Verification and policy
subsystems.role: checks presented credentials and applies access rules before letting an agent act.

subsystems.name: Trust registry
subsystems.role: lists trusted issuers and tracks revoked credentials.

subsystems.name: Audit trail
subsystems.role: records which agent did what, with proof, for accountability.

buildSteps.title: Define credential schemas
buildSteps.detail: Decide what an agent identity credential must contain: who created it, what it is allowed to do, under whose authority, and when it expires.

buildSteps.title: Establish governance
buildSteps.detail: Agree on a trust framework: which entities may issue credentials, how disputes are handled, and how issuers are held accountable.

buildSteps.title: Implement a DID method
buildSteps.detail: Choose or create a decentralized identifier method suited to agents and build a resolver that maps identifiers to public keys and service endpoints.

buildSteps.title: Build issuance service
buildSteps.detail: Create software for trusted authorities to sign and issue verifiable credentials to agents, with revocation hooks.

buildSteps.title: Build agent wallet
buildSteps.detail: Integrate secure key storage and credential presentation into agent runtimes, so an agent can prove its identity without a human in the loop.

buildSteps.title: Add verification hooks
buildSteps.detail: Embed credential verification into API gateways, message brokers, and agent-to-agent communication protocols.

buildSteps.title: Deploy trust registry and revocation
buildSteps.detail: Run a live service that lets verifiers check whether an issuer is trusted and whether a credential has been revoked.

buildSteps.title: Pilot and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Run agents through real workflows, test interoperability and attack resistance, then feed results back into standards.

prerequisites.why: provides a standard way to give agents self-owned identifiers that do not depend on a single platform.
standard data model for signed, tamper-evident claims that can be checked without contacting the issuer.

prerequisites.tech: Public key infrastructure and secure key management
prerequisites.why: agents need hardware-backed or software-protected keys to sign and prove possession.

prerequisites.tech: Agent communication protocols with identity hooks
prerequisites.why: most agent protocols today lack native identity and authentication layers, so proofing must be bolted on.
needed to prove authority or provenance without revealing sensitive agent internals or user data.
without common schemas, credentials cannot be interpreted consistently across different systems.

pathway.milestone: DIDs and VCs are standardized for people and organisations; first experiments apply them to AI agents.
pathway.unlocks: a cryptographic basis for machine identity that does not rely on shared secrets.

pathway.milestone: Enterprise pilots where agents present verifiable credentials to APIs and other agents.
pathway.unlocks: auditable, least-privilege access for autonomous workflows.

pathway.milestone: Cross-vendor trust registries and revocation lists become interoperable.
pathway.unlocks: agents from different providers can trust each other without bilateral contracts.

pathway.milestone: Autonomous agents negotiate and prove identity and authority without human setup.
pathway.unlocks: safe multi-agent economies and delegated workflows at scale.
